chapters.t: In the beginning was the Word. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
Everything that exists was made through him.
In him was life, and that life was the light of everyone.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has never put it out.
And the Word became a person and lived among us, full of grace and truth.
There was a wedding in a village called Cana, and Jesus was invited.
Half way through the party the wine ran out, which was terribly embarrassing.
Jesus’ mother told him, and Jesus said to the servants, “Fill those jars with water.”
They filled six big stone jars right to the brim.
“Now take some to the master of the feast,” said Jesus.
He tasted it — and it was wine, the best of the whole day. It was Jesus’ first sign.
One night a teacher named Nicodemus came quietly to talk with Jesus.
“Teacher,” he said, “we know that God has sent you.”
Jesus answered, “To see God’s kingdom, a person must be born all over again.”
Nicodemus was puzzled. “How can that happen when someone is old?”
“For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son,” said Jesus.
“Whoever believes in him will not be lost, but will have life for ever.”
Jesus was tired from walking, and sat down beside a well at noon.
A woman came to draw water, and Jesus asked her for a drink.
She was surprised, because people like him usually did not speak to people like her.
“If you knew who was asking,” said Jesus, “you would ask him for living water.”
“Whoever drinks the water I give will never be thirsty again.”
The woman ran back to her town and told everyone she had met him.
By a pool in Jerusalem lay many people who were ill.
One man had not been able to walk for thirty-eight years.
Jesus asked him, “Do you want to get well?”
“I have no one to help me into the water,” the man answered sadly.
Jesus said, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.” And at once he could.
A huge crowd followed Jesus, and by evening everyone was hungry.
A boy had five small loaves and two little fish — and that was all there was.
Jesus took the bread, thanked God, and began to share it out.
Everybody ate as much as they wanted — more than five thousand people.
Afterwards they gathered up twelve baskets of leftovers.
Jesus said, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry.”
At a great festival, Jesus stood up and spoke to the crowds.
“If anyone is thirsty, let them come to me and drink,” he called.
Some people said, “This really is the one God promised.”
Others argued and were not sure at all.
Even the guards sent to arrest him came back saying, “Nobody ever spoke like this man.”
Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.”
“Whoever follows me will never walk in the dark.”
Some people brought a woman who had done wrong, hoping to trap him.
Jesus bent down and wrote in the dust with his finger.
“Whoever has never done anything wrong may throw the first stone,” he said.
One by one they all walked away, and Jesus said kindly, “Go, and live a new life.”
Jesus saw a man who had been blind since the day he was born.
He made a little mud and gently put it on the man’s eyes.
“Go and wash in the pool,” said Jesus. The man went, and washed.
He came back seeing! His neighbours could hardly believe it was the same man.
“One thing I know,” he told them. “I was blind, and now I can see.”
Jesus said, “I am the good shepherd, and I know my sheep by name.”
“My sheep know my voice, and they follow me.”
“A hired man runs away when a wolf comes, because the sheep are not his.”
“But the good shepherd gives his own life for the sheep.”
“And no one can ever snatch them out of my hand.”
Jesus had three dear friends: Mary, Martha, and their brother Lazarus.
Lazarus became very ill, and by the time Jesus arrived he had died.
Martha said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would still be alive.”
Jesus wept with them. He loved them, and he was sad too.
“I am the resurrection and the life,” he said. “Whoever believes in me will live.”
They rolled the stone away, and Jesus called, “Lazarus, come out!”
And out he came, alive again. Everyone was amazed.
Mary poured a jar of costly perfume over Jesus’ feet, and the whole house smelled sweet.
“That could have been sold to help the poor,” grumbled Judas.
“Leave her alone,” said Jesus. “She has done a beautiful thing.”
The next day Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a young donkey.
Crowds waved palm branches and shouted for joy as he passed.
At supper Jesus stood up, took off his coat, and tied a towel round his waist.
He poured water into a bowl and began to wash his friends’ dusty feet.
“You shall never wash my feet!” said Peter. But Jesus showed him why it mattered.
“I am your teacher, and I have washed your feet. Now do the same for one another.”
“Love one another. That is how everyone will know you belong to me.”
“Do not let your hearts be troubled,” said Jesus. “Trust God, and trust me.”
“In my Father’s house there is plenty of room, and I am going to prepare a place for you.”
Thomas asked, “But we do not know the way!”
Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth and the life.”
“I will not leave you on your own. I will send a Helper to be with you always.”
“I am the vine,” said Jesus, “and you are the branches.”
“A branch cannot grow fruit by itself. It has to stay joined to the vine.”
“Stay close to me, and you will bear a great deal of fruit.”
“Love each other the way I have loved you.”
“There is no greater love than to give your life for your friends.”
“Soon you will be very sad,” said Jesus, “but your sadness will turn into joy.”
“It is like a mother who forgets her pain once her child is born.”
“I will see you again, and no one will be able to take your joy away.”
“In this world you will have trouble — but be brave. I have overcome the world.”
Then Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed for his friends.
“Father, keep them safe, and keep them together.”
“I am not asking you to take them out of the world, only to protect them.”
“And I pray for everyone who will ever believe because of them.”
That night soldiers came to the garden with lanterns and swords.
Peter drew a sword, but Jesus told him to put it away.
They led Jesus away, and Peter followed a long way behind.
Three times people asked Peter, “Are you his friend?” and three times he said no.
Pilate asked Jesus, “Are you a king?” Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world.”
The soldiers were cruel to Jesus, and Pilate handed him over.
They led him to a hill, and there he was crucified between two others.
His mother stood nearby, and Jesus asked his friend to take care of her.
Jesus said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head.
His friends laid him gently in a new tomb cut out of the rock.
Very early on Sunday morning, Mary came to the tomb while it was still dark.
The great stone had been rolled away, and the tomb was empty!
Mary stood outside crying, because she thought someone had taken him away.
Someone said gently, “Mary.” She knew that voice at once. It was Jesus, alive!
Thomas would not believe until he saw for himself — and then he said, “My Lord and my God!”
Jesus said, “Happy are those who have not seen, and yet believe.”
Later, some of the friends went fishing all night and caught nothing at all.
At dawn a man on the shore called, “Try the other side of the boat.”
The net came up so full of fish they could hardly pull it in. “It is the Lord!” said John.
Jesus had already made a fire on the beach, with breakfast waiting.
Three times he asked Peter, “Do you love me?” Three times Peter said yes.
“Then take care of my sheep,” said Jesus. And Peter was forgiven, and glad.
